title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 112
paragraphs: To the herdsman it seemed, the case standing thus, that his wife spoke well, and at once he did so. The child he was carrying to put to death he handed over to his wife, and his own dead child he took and placed in the chest in which he had been carrying the other. Having adorned it with all the ornaments of the other child, he bore it to the most desolate part of the mountains and left it there. And when the third day came after the child had been exposed, the herdsman went to the city, leaving one of his under-herdsmen to keep watch there, and when he came to the house of Harpagos he said that he was ready to display the dead body of the child. Harpagos sent the most trusted of his spearmen, and through them saw and buried the herdsman's child. This child then had its burial; but the one who was afterwards called Cyrus the herdsman's wife had received, and was bringing him up, giving him no doubt some other name, not Cyrus.
